question: to the Commission Nadine Morano (PPE) Subject:

The heatwave that has affected Europe since June 2026 illustrates the worsening risks associated with climate change. According to the World Health Organisation, it had already caused more than 1 000 deaths by 30 June 20261. Eurostat figures show that annual household energy consumption for cooling has almost doubled in the EU since 2015. While cooling still accounted for only 0.8% of the EU’s final energy consumption in 20242, heatwaves are driving up electricity demand, putting increasing pressure on energy grids and markets. As Europe gets hotter, air conditioning is becoming less and less about comfort and more a public health issue of protecting the most vulnerable. As a consequence, we need to adapt buildings to cope with heatwaves, encourage the installation of efficient, energy-saving airconditioning systems – alongside passive cooling solutions – and ensure that the electricity infrastructure can meet the growing demand for cooling. Does the Commission intend to support Member States in developing sustainable airconditioning solutions and adapting electricity grids to meet the foreseeable increase in cooling needs?
